newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Huge harvest weekend ahead.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Huge harvest weekend ahead.

text.p: Mostly dry, warm weather conditions should allow harvesting to advance rapidly this weekend across Oklahoma and southern Kansas, grain dealers said Friday.
"We've got the biggest harvest weekend of the season ahead of us," an Oklahoma dealer said.

"It's supposed to be 99 (degrees Farenheit) in Wichita today. Humidity may be a little high but we're also supposed to be getting some winds that'll help dry down the crop," a south central Kansas dealer said. "All in all, that's nearly ideal harvest weather."
Dealers said they were still hearing reports of larger-than-expected yields in northern Oklahoma and southern Kansas.
"We've heard anywhere from 10 to 83 (bushels per acre). That 83 was on a field just east of Enid (Okla.). There have been a lot of 48s and 50s," an Oklahoma dealer said.
Another Oklahoma dealer said he had heard about the 83-bushel field, and said he knew of a 300-acre field in Garber, Okla. that scored an average of 76 bushels per acre.
Agronomists cautioned Thursday against making sweeping judgments about the size of this year's crop because it is still early in the harvest cycle.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
